title: Pseudo-coherence is equivalent to m-pseudo-coherence for every m
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $D(R)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $R$-modules. For an integer $m$, call an object $C$ of $D(R)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(R)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Call $C$ pseudo-coherent if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. Let $C$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules, viewed as an object of $D(R)$. Then $C$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (Tag 064U), equivalence of pseudo-coherence and m-pseudo-coherence for every m

proof.text: Given a bounded above finite free representative E and its derived isomorphism to C, take the brutal truncation of E in degrees at least m. Define its inclusion degreewise by the canonical term isomorphisms in degrees at least m and zero below m. The three component maps computing cohomology are isomorphisms above m, so the induced cohomology map is an isomorphism. At m, the middle and next maps are isomorphisms, hence the cycles map is an isomorphism and the homology map is epi. The truncation is bounded and finite free, including when m exceeds the upper bound. Transport its map through Q and compose with the derived isomorphism to C. This is the required m-pseudo-coherent witness.
For the converse, write E to C for the degree-zero approximation with upper term bound b. Above max(b,0), E has zero cohomology and its map induces an isomorphism, so C has zero cohomology.

For any bounded finite free complex F and chain map g:F to C, the identity on F witnesses (n+1)-pseudo-coherence. Apply the first clause of the distinguished-triangle lemma to the mapping-cone triangle at n and use the assumed n-pseudo-coherence of C. This gives n-pseudo-coherence of Cone(g). If its cohomology vanishes above n, the finite-cohomology lemma gives finite generation of H^n(Cone(g)). Thus the finite-cone hypothesis of the construction lemma holds.

When R fits in the module universe, apply the finite-cone free-model construction to C, its upper cohomology bound and the finite cone groups proved in the preceding step. It yields a bounded above finite free F with a chain-level quasi-isomorphism g:F to C. Q sends g to an isomorphism, giving the defining pseudo-coherent representative.

For completeness with independent universes, if R does not fit in the module universe, every free module M there is zero. Otherwise a nontrivial free M has faithful scalar action; R injects into the function type M to M by scalar multiplication, contradicting the size assumption. Thus every approximation E is termwise zero. For each i use the (i-1)-approximation to force H^i(C)=0. The zero map from the zero complex to C is a quasi-isomorphism, so the zero complex gives a bounded above finite free representative.
